title: Role-fit heuristics — Senior Serving Runtime candidate
content:
Quick scratchpad after loop with candidate (senior runtime engineer). Not polished — notes to self + items to validate before debrief.

High-level impression:
- Very strong intuition about cache/kv tradeoffs and per-request memory patterns. Spoke convincingly about eviction policies and when to prefer prefix caching vs per-session KV retention.
- Solid low-level understanding of quantized kernels and where FP16 vs q4 impact latency. Could explain spill behavior when attention memory exceeds GPU RAM.
- Took a bit to articulate routing/fallback policies end-to-end (could map to our smart routing doc but needed prompting).
- Communication: pragmatic and thoughtful, not flashy; good at saying "I don't know" and proposing experiments.

Pairing exercise (30m):
- Task: optimize a toy inference loop for batched chat with mixed sequence lengths.
- Candidate changed batching strategy: grouped by prefix hash and then by length bucket -> improved median latency in thought experiment. Wrote pseudo-code for dynamic batch windows.
- Implemented a quick KV cache cleanup patch (conceptually correct), but missed a subtle race condition around cache invalidation on concurrent flush -> flagged for follow-up.
- Outcome: passed pairing with two small action items (see follow-ups).

Strengths:
- Deep debugging mentality (logs-first).
- Good mental model for memory/per-token cost and how batching impacts tail latency.
- Experience with on-prem deployment constraints (e.g., limited host RAM, HSM/KMS integration).

Red flags / concerns:
- Limited production telemetry background; asked for clarifications about distributed tracing tradeoffs. Could pair with SRE on concrete examples.
- Little recent exposure to Triton internals (has used Triton but not contributed) — acceptable but a gap for certain kernel-level tasks.

Rough score (1–5, 5 strong):
- System design / architecture: 4
- Low-level performance optimization: 4
- Telemetry & observability: 3
- Communication / culture fit: 4
- Overall hire recommend: strong maybe (4) — leaning toward hire if follow-ups validate concurrency edge case thinking.

Follow-ups / essential checks before final decision:
- Ask candidate to write a 1–2 page mini-design: "KV cache invalidation in a multitenant serving runtime" (due +3 days). Goal: verify race-condition handling and invariants.
- Run a short take-home micro-bench: given repo snippet, add length-bucketing batching and measure median and p95 latency (2–4 hours).
- Pair with SRE/observability to discuss tracing strategy for batching (30m).
- Verify prior infra contributions (link to PRs) — candidate claims kernel patches; dig into commit history (PR link above).

Open questions I still have:
- How comfortable are they with large-scale rollout patterns (canary + progressive routing)? They described rollout ideas but couldn't map to our console controls.
- How well do they understand quantization accuracy regressions and tooling to surface them? Gave some heuristics but wants to learn more.

Decision suggestion for hiring committee:
- Move forward to take-home + SRE pair; if take-home shows correct concurrency handling and the mini-bench shows sensible latency wins, extend offer for senior runtime engineer. Consider slightly higher compensation for kernel/quantization expertise.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Capture exact pairing code snippets and the failing concurrency scenario (line numbers) before sending to candidate.
- Quick DM to Diego about SRE pairing availability next Thurs.
- Mark INF-4821 as follow-up ticket to capture hiring artifacts and outcome.

End of note.
